section_name: Evaluation Methodology: Error Metrics and In-Sample Resubstitution Limits

candidates.title: How Biased Is the Apparent Error Rate of a Prediction Rule?
candidates.reason: Establishes the fundamental optimism theorem showing that evaluating prediction errors on the identical observations used for estimation produces a downwardly biased apparent error, formalizing the covariance penalty required to reflect out-of-sample error.

candidates.title: Estimating the Error Rate of a Prediction Rule: Improvement on Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Analyzes the statistical discrepancy between apparent training error and generalization error, demonstrating why in-sample resubstitution yields an overly optimistic evaluation and proposing resampling principles to estimate true performance.

candidates.title: The Estimation of Prediction Error: Covariance Penalties and Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Provides a comprehensive mathematical framework connecting in-sample mean squared error, degrees of freedom, and expected out-of-sample prediction error through covariance penalties.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: Foundational methodology paper establishing that assessing predictors on observations used in their estimation yields invalid evaluations, formalizing sample-reuse and hold-out evaluation principles.

candidates.title: The Predictive Sample Reuse Method with Applications
candidates.reason: Demonstrates why training sample resubstitution error cannot validate predictive performance and develops predictive sample-reuse methodology to assess accuracy on genuinely held-out observations.

candidates.title: Advantages of the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) Over the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) in Assessing Average Model Performance
candidates.reason: Examines the methodological distinction between MAE and RMSE/MSE, demonstrating that squared error criteria confound average error magnitude with residual dispersion and sample size.

candidates.title: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) or Mean Absolute Error (MAE)? – Arguments Against Avoiding RMSE in the Literature
candidates.reason: Analyzes the statistical and distributional assumptions underlying MSE/RMSE versus MAE, detailing how squared error metrics correspond directly to Gaussian error assumptions whereas absolute errors assume Laplacian error distributions.

candidates.title: Root-mean-square error (RMSE) or mean absolute error (MAE): when to use them or not
candidates.reason: Synthesizes the methodological debate surrounding MAE and RMSE/MSE, demonstrating how the choice of evaluation metric reflects specific assumptions about residual distributions and error penalties.

candidates.title: Error Measures For Generalizing About Forecasting Methods: Empirical Comparisons
candidates.reason: Empirically evaluates the validity, outlier sensitivity, and reliability of mean squared error, mean absolute error, and relative measures when assessing predictive performance.

candidates.title: Another Look at Measures of Forecast Accuracy
candidates.reason: Critiques foundational accuracy metrics, outlining the mathematical limitations, degeneracy issues, and statistical properties of standard squared and absolute error metrics in predictive evaluation.

candidates.title: Some Comments on Cp
candidates.reason: Demonstrates how fitting parameters to training observations mechanically reduces the in-sample residual sum of squares, formulating the Cp statistic to penalize training-set optimism.

candidates.title: Submodel Selection and Evaluation in Regression. The X-Random Case
candidates.reason: Investigates the breakdown between in-sample goodness-of-fit metrics and true predictive error, proving that in-sample error evaluations severely underestimate prediction risk.

candidates.title: Statistics for the Evaluation and Comparison of Models
candidates.reason: Presents rigorous difference-measure methodology (MAE, RMSE, residual decomposition) and clarifies the limitations of drawing inferential or uncertainty claims from deterministic in-sample fits.

candidates.title: On Measuring and Correcting the Effects of Data Mining and Model Selection
candidates.reason: Formalizes generalized degrees of freedom to quantify the optimism induced when fitted corrections adapt to training observations, directly linking parameter fitting to apparent residual reduction.
